body.text: dhana-ṛṇa-ṣaṣ-vidham
body.translated_text: The six operations with positive and negative numbers

children.text: utpādakam yad pravadanti buddhes adhiṣṭhitam sat-puruṣeṇa sāṃkhyās/
children.translated_text: That which the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> declare to be the producer of intellect, presided over by the Supreme Person (<s>sat-puruṣa</s>),

children.text: vyaktasya kṛtsnasya tad eka-bījam avyaktam īśam gaṇitam ca vande//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: that sole seed of all the manifest [world], the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) Lord — and mathematics — I salute.

children.text: pūrvam proktam vyaktam avyakta-bījam prāyas praśnās no vinā avyakta-yuktyā/
children.translated_text: Previously, manifest [arithmetic] was taught, [which is] the seed of the unmanifest [algebra]. Most problems, without the method of the unmanifest [algebra],

children.text: jñātum śakyās manda-dhībhis nitāntam yasmāt tasmāt vacmi bīja-kriyām ca//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: cannot be known at all by those of dull intellect; therefore I teach <s>bīja-kriyā</s> (algebra) as well.

body.text: yoge yutis syāt kṣayayos svayos vā dhana-ṛṇayos antaram eva yogas/
body.translated_text: In addition, the sum of two negatives or two positives [is their total]; for a positive and a negative, the addition is merely the difference.

children.text: rūpa-trayam rūpa-catuṣṭayam ca kṣayam dhanam vā sahitam vada āśu//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Three units and four units, whether negative or positive — tell their sum quickly.

children.text: sva-ṛṇam kṣayam svam ca pṛthak-pṛthaktve dhana-ṛṇayos sṃkalanām avaiṣi//[upajāti-ab; cd=7]
children.translated_text: A negative of a positive is negative, and a positive [remains] positive when [taken] separately — thus you understand the addition of positive and negative [numbers].

body.text: atra rūpāṇām avyaktānām ca ādya-akṣarāṇi upalakṣaṇa-artham lekhyāni/ tathā yāni ūna-gatāni tāni ūrdhva-bindūni ca iti//[prose]
body.translated_text: Here, the initial letters of numbers and unknowns are to be written as symbols. Likewise, those which are negative have dots placed above them.

body.text: evam bhinneṣu api iti//[prose]
body.translated_text: Similarly for fractions also.

body.text: saṃśodhyamānam svam ṛṇatvam eti svatvam kṣayas tad-yutis uktavat ca//[upajāti-cd; ab=4cd]
body.translated_text: That which is being subtracted changes its sign: a positive becomes negative and a negative becomes positive; and then addition is performed as stated before.

body.text: trayāt dvayam svāt svam ṛṇāt ṛṇam ca vyastam ca saṃśodhya vada āśu śeṣam//[upajāti-ab; cd=10]
body.translated_text: From three [subtract] two — positive from positive, and negative from negative — and also reversed; tell quickly the remainder after subtraction.

body.text: svayos asvayos svam vadhas sva-ṛṇa-ghāte kṣayas//[bhujaṅgaprayāta-a (+2akṣara); b=11; cd=13]
body.translated_text: The product of two positives or two negatives is positive; the product of a positive and a negative is negative.

body.text: dhanam dhanena ṛṇam ṛṇena nighnam dvayam trayeṇa svam ṛṇena kim syāt//[upajāti-cd; ab=8]
body.translated_text: Positive multiplied by positive, negative by negative; two by three, positive by negative — what would be [the result]?

body.text: bhāga-hāre api ca evam niruktam//[bhujaṅgaprayāta-b (-2akṣara); a=9; cd=13]
body.translated_text: In division also it is stated likewise.

children.text: rūpa-aṣṭakam rūpa-catuṣṭayena dhanam dhanena ṛṇam ṛṇena bhaktam/
children.translated_text: Eight units divided by four units — positive by positive, negative by negative;

children.text: ṛṇam dhanena svam ṛṇena kim syāt drutam vada idam yadi bobudhīṣi//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: negative by positive, positive by negative — what would be [the result]? Tell this quickly if you wish to learn.

body.text: kṛtis sva-ṛṇayos svam sva-mūle dhana-ṛṇe na mūlam kṣayasya asti tasya akṛtitvāt//[bhujaṅgaprayāta-cd; a=9; b=11]
body.translated_text: The square of a positive or negative is positive; the square roots [of a positive number] are positive and negative. There is no square root of a negative number, because it is not a [perfect] square.

body.text: dhanasya rūpa-tritayasya vargam kṣayasya ca brūhi sakhe mama āśu/
body.translated_text: Tell me quickly, friend, the square of positive three units and of negative [three units],

body.text: dhana-ātmakānām adhana-ātmakānām mūlam navānām ca pṛthak vada āśu//[upajāti]
body.translated_text: and tell separately the square root of nine, [considered as] positive and as negative, quickly.

body.text: śūnya-ṣaṣ-vidham
body.translated_text: The six operations with zero

body.text: kha-yoge viyoge dhana-ṛṇam tathā eva cyutam śūnya-tas tad-viparyāsam eti//[bhujaṅgaprayāta-ab; cd=18]
body.translated_text: In addition with zero and subtraction [of zero], a positive or negative [number remains] as it is. [A number] subtracted from zero becomes its opposite.

body.text: rūoa-trayam svam kṣaya-gam ca kham ca kim syāt kha-yuktam vada kha-cyutam ca//[indravajrā-ab; cd=19]
body.translated_text: Three units — positive, negative, and zero — what would each be when added to zero? Tell also when zero is subtracted.

body.text: vadha-ādau viyat khasya kham khena ghāte kha-hāras bhavet khena bhaktas ca rāśis//[bhujaṅgaprayāta-cd; ab=16]
body.translated_text: In multiplication and other [operations, a number multiplied by zero gives] zero; zero multiplied by zero is zero. A quantity divided by zero becomes <s>kha-hāra</s> (a quantity with zero as divisor).

body.text: dvi-ghnam tri-hṛt kham kha-hṛtam trayam ca śūnyasya vargam vada me padam ca//[indravajrā-cd; ab=17]
body.translated_text: Tell me: zero multiplied by two, divided by three; and three divided by zero; and the square and square root of zero.

children.text: asmin vikāras kha-hareṇa rāśau api praviṣṭeṣu api niḥsṛteṣu/
children.translated_text: In a quantity with zero as divisor (<s>kha-hara</s>), there is no change even when [other] quantities enter or depart —

children.text: bahuṣu api syāt laya-sṛṣṭi-kāle anante acyute bhbūta0gaṇeṣu yad-vat//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: just as at the time of cosmic dissolution (<s>laya</s>) and creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), [there is no change] in the Infinite (<s>Ananta</s>) and Imperishable (<s>Acyuta</s>) [Lord], though the multitudes of beings [come and go].

body.text: varṇa-ṣaṣ-vidham
body.translated_text: The six operations with unknowns (<s>varṇa</s>)

children.text: yāvattāvat-kālakas nīlakas anyas varṇas pītas lohitas ca etad-ādyās/
children.translated_text: <s>Yāvattāvat</s>, <s>kālaka</s> (black), <s>nīlaka</s> (blue), and other colors — yellow, red, and so forth —

children.text: avyaktānām kalpitās māna-saṃjñās tad-saṃkhyānam kartum ācārya-varyais//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: these have been devised by eminent teachers as designations for unknowns, in order to compute with them.

body.text: yogas antaram teṣu samāna-jātyos vibhinna-jātyos ca pṛthak sthitis ca//[upajāti-ab; cd=26ab]
body.translated_text: The sum and difference [operate] among those of the same kind; for those of different kinds, they remain separate.

children.text: svam avyaktam ekam sakhe sa-eka-rūpam dhana-avyakta-yugmam vi-rūpa-aṣṭakam ca/
children.translated_text: One positive unknown, friend, with one unit; and two positive unknowns minus eight units;

children.text: yutau pakṣayos etayos kim dhana-ṛṇe viparyasya ca aikye bhavet kim vada āśu//[bhujaṅgaprayāta]
children.translated_text: what is the sum of these two sides, [each being] positive and negative? And reversing [the signs], what would be the sum? Tell quickly.

body.text: dhana-avyakta-varga-trayam sa-tri-rūpam kṣaya-avyakta-yugmena yuktam ca kim syāt//[bhujaṅgaprayāta-ab; cd=25]
body.translated_text: Three positive squares of the unknown with three units — added to two negative unknowns, what would be [the result]?

body.text: dhana-avyakta-yugmāt ṛṇa-avyakta-ṣaṭkam sa-rūpa-aṣṭakam projjhya śeṣam vada āśu//[bhujaṅgaprayāta-cd; ab=24]
body.translated_text: From two positive unknowns, subtract six negative unknowns with eight units; tell the remainder quickly.

children.text: syāt rūpa-varṇa-abhihatau tu varṇas dvi-tri-ādikānām sama-jātikānām//[upajāti-cd; ab=22]
children.translated_text: When a number is multiplied by an unknown, the result is the unknown [with that coefficient]; for two, three, and so on of the same kind,

children.text: vadhe tu tad-varga-ghana-ādayas syus tad-bhāvitam ca asama-jāti-ghāte/
children.translated_text: in multiplication, their squares, cubes, and so on arise; in the product of unlike kinds, it is called <s>bhāvita</s> (product).

children.text: bhāga-ādikam rūpa-vat eva śeṣam vyakte yad uktam gaṇite tad atra//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Division and the rest are just as for numbers; what was stated in manifest arithmetic (<s>vyakta-gaṇita</s>) applies here.

children.text: guṇyas pṛthak guṇa-khaṇḍa-samas niveśyas tais khaṇḍakais krama-hatas sahitas yathā-uktyā/
children.translated_text: The multiplicand is to be set down separately as many times as there are parts of the multiplier; [then] multiplied in order by those parts and combined as stated.

children.text: avyakta-varga-karaṇī-guṇanāsu cintyas vyakta-ukta-khaṇḍa-guṇanā-vidhis evam atra//[vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: In multiplications involving squares of unknowns and surds, the method of multiplication by parts as stated in manifest [arithmetic] is to be followed here as well.

children.text: yāvattāvat-pañcakam vi-eka-rūpam yāvattāvadbhis tribhis sa-dvi-rūpais/
children.translated_text: Five <s>yāvattāvats</s> minus one unit, [multiplied] by three <s>yāvattāvats</s> with two units;

children.text: saṃguṇya drāk brūhi guṇyam guṇam vā vyastam sva-ṛṇam kalpayitvā ca vidvan//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: having multiplied, tell quickly — whether [taking] the multiplicand or multiplier reversed, assigning positive and negative [signs], O learned one.

children.text: bhājyāt chedas śudhyati pracyutas san sveṣu sthānakeṣu krameṇa/
children.translated_text: The divisor is removed from the dividend and divides out in its own places successively;

children.text: yais yais varṇais saṃguṇas yais ca rūpais bhāga-hāre labdhayas tās syus atra//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: by whichever unknowns and whichever numbers [the divisor was] multiplied, those are the quotients in the division here.

body.text: rūpais ṣaḍbhis varjitānām caturṇām avyaktānām brūhi vargam sakhe me/[śālinī-ab]
body.translated_text: Tell me, friend, the square of four unknowns minus six units.

children.text: kṛtibhyas ādāya padāni teṣām dvayos dvayos ca abhihatim dvi-nighnīm/
children.translated_text: Taking the square roots from the squares [of the terms], and the product of each pair doubled,

children.text: śeṣāt tyajet rūpa-padam gṛhītvā ced santi rūpāṇi tathā eva śeṣam//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: one should subtract from the remainder, taking the square root of the number [term] if there are numbers; similarly for the rest.

children.text: yāvattāvat-kālaka-nīlaka-varṇās tri-pañca-sapta-dhanam/
children.translated_text: The unknowns <s>yāvattāvat</s>, <s>kālaka</s>, and <s>nīlaka</s> — [with coefficients] three, five, and seven positive,

children.text: dvi-tri-eka-mitais kṣaya-gais sahitās rahitās kati syus tais//[āryā]
children.translated_text: combined with and separated from [those having coefficients] two, three, and one negative [respectively] — what would they be?

children.text: yāvattāvat-trayam ṛṇam ṛṇam kālakau nīlakas svam rūpeṇa āḍhyās dvi-guṇita-mitais tais tu tais eva nighnās/
children.translated_text: Three <s>yāvattāvats</s> negative, two <s>kālakas</s> negative, one <s>nīlaka</s> positive, each increased by a unit, multiplied by those same [expressions] doubled,

children.text: kim syāt teṣām guṇana-ja-phalam guṇya-bhaktam ca kim syāt guṇyasya atha prakathaya kṛtim mūlam asyās kṛtes ca//[mandākrāntā]
children.translated_text: what would be the product of their multiplication? And what would be [the product] divided by the multiplicand? Then tell the square of the multiplicand and the square root of that square.

body.text: karaṇī-ṣaṣ-vidham
body.translated_text: The six operations with surds (<s>karaṇī</s>)

children.text: yogam karaṇyos mahatīm prakalpya ghātasya mūlam dvi-guṇam laghum ca/
children.translated_text: Having found the sum of two surds as the greater [quantity], and twice the square root of their product as the lesser,

children.text: yoga-antare rūpa-vat etayos te vargeṇa vargam guṇayet bhajet ca//[indravajrā]
children.translated_text: [apply] the sum and difference just as for numbers; the square [of surds] one should multiply by a square, and divide [likewise].

children.text: laghvyā hṛtāyās tu padam mahatyā sa-ekam nir-ekam sva-hatam laghu-ghnam/
children.translated_text: The square root of the greater [surd] divided by the lesser, plus one and minus one, each squared and multiplied by the lesser,

children.text: yoga-antare stas kramaśas tayos vā pṛthak-sthitis syāt yadi na asti mūlam//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: give the sum and difference [of the two surds] respectively; or they remain separate if no [rational] square root exists.

children.text: dvika-aṣṭa-mityos tri-bha-saṃkhyayos ca yoga-antare brūhi sakhe karaṇyos/ BH 35c/ tri-sapta-mityos ca ciram vicintya ced ṣaṣ-vidham vetsi sakhe karaṇyās//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Tell, friend, the sum and difference of surds [measuring] two and eight, and of [surds measuring] three and twenty-seven; and of three and seven — having reflected long, if you know the six operations of surds, friend.

children.text: dvi-tri-aṣṭa-saṃkhyā-guṇakas karaṇyos guṇyas tri-saṃkhyā ca sa-pañca-rūpā/
children.translated_text: Of surds with multipliers numbered two, three, and eight: the multiplicand is [a surd of] three with five units;

children.text: vadham pracakṣva āśu vi-pañca-rūpe guṇe atha vā tri-arka-mite karaṇyau//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: tell the product quickly when the multiplier is minus five units; or when the surds measure three and twelve.

children.text: kṣayas bhavet ca kṣaya-rūpa-vargas ced sādhyate asau karaṇītva-hetos/ BH 37c/ ṛṇa-ātnikāyās ca tathā karaṇyās mūlam kṣayas rūpa-vidhāna-hetos//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: A negative [number], when squared, yields a positive square; this is established for the properties of surds. And of a negative surd, the square root is taken as negative, for the purpose of [mathematical] operations.

children.text: dhana-ṛṇa-tā-vyatyayam īpsitāyās chede karaṇyās asakṛt vidhāya/
children.translated_text: Having repeatedly changed the sign (positive to negative or vice versa) of the desired surd in the divisor,

children.text: tādṛś chidā bhājya-harau nihanyāt ekā eva yāvat karaṇī hare syāt//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: one should multiply both dividend and divisor by such a [modified] divisor until only one surd remains in the divisor.

children.text: bhājyās tayā bhājya-gatās karaṇyas labdhās karaṇyas yadi yoga-jās syus/ BH 38g/ viśleṣa-sūtreṇa pṛthak ca kāryā yathā tathā praṣṭus abhīpsitās syus//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: The surds in the dividend, divided by that [remaining surd in the divisor], give the quotient surds. If [the quotient surds] arise from addition, they should be separated by the rule of subtraction, so as to obtain the desired [form].

children.text: vargeṇa yoga-karaṇī vihṛtā viśudhyet khaṇḍāni tad-kṛti-padasya yathā-īpsitāni/
children.translated_text: When a compound surd is divided by a square, it is simplified; the parts [are found] from the square root of the square [of the compound surd] as desired.

children.text: kṛtvā tadīya-kṛtayas khalu pūrva-labdhyā kṣuṇṇās bhavanti pṛthak evam imās karaṇyas//[vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: Having done so, the squares of those [parts], multiplied by the previously obtained [quotient], become the individual surds.

children.text: dvika-tri-pañca-pramitās karaṇyas tāsām kṛtim dvi-trika-saṃkhyayos ca/
children.translated_text: Surds measuring two, three, and five — tell their square, and [the square] of [surds measuring] two and three;

children.text: ṣaṣ-pañcaka-dvi-trika-saṃmitānām pṛthak pṛthak me kathaya āśu vidvan//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: and of [surds] measuring six, five, two, and three — tell me each one separately, quickly, O learned one.

children.text: aṣṭādaśa-aṣṭa-dvika-saṃmitānām kṛtī kṛtīnām ca sakhe padāni//[upajāti-ab; cd=43ab]
children.translated_text: And, friend, the square roots of the squares of [surds] measuring eighteen, eight, and two.

children.text: varge karaṇyās yadi vā karaṇyos tulyāni rūpāṇi atha vā bahūnām/
children.translated_text: If in the square of a surd, or of two surds, or of many [surds], the numbers are equal,

children.text: viśodhayet rūpa-kṛtes padena śeṣasya rūpāṇi yuta-ūnitāni//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: one should subtract from the number by the square root of [the remaining] number's square; the numbers of the remainder, increased and diminished [by that root],

children.text: pṛthak tad-ardhe karaṇī-dvayam syāt mūle atha bahvī karaṇī tayos yā/
children.translated_text: each halved, give the two surds [as the square root]. Then, if there are many surds, that one of the two which

children.text: rūpāṇi tāni evam atas api bhūyas śeṣās karaṇyas yadi santi varge//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: has numbers — thus, further again, the remaining surds, if there are [more] in the square [are treated similarly].

children.text: ṛṇa-ātmikā ced karaṇī kṛtau syāt dhana-ātmikām tām parikalpya sādhye/
children.translated_text: If a surd in the square is negative, it should be assumed as positive for the purpose of the solution.

children.text: mūle karaṇyau anayos abhīṣṭā kṣaya-ātmikā ekā su-dhiyā avagamyā//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Of these two surds in the [square] root, the desired one is to be understood by the wise as negative.

children.text: tri-sapta-mityos vada me karaṇyos viśleṣa-vargam kṛtitas padam ca/[upajāti-cd; ab=40ef]
children.translated_text: Tell me the square of the difference of two surds (<s>karaṇīs</s>) measuring three and seven, and the root of that square.

children.text: dvika-tri-pañca-pramitās karaṇyas sva-sva-ṛṇa-gās vyasta-dhana-ṛṇa-gās vā/
children.translated_text: If surds measuring two, three, and five, each positive or negative, or with reversed positive and negative signs —

children.text: tāsām kṛtim brūhi kṛtes padam ca ced ṣaṣ-vidham vetsi sakhe karaṇyās//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: tell their square and the root of the square, if you know the sixfold [operations] of surds, friend.

children.text: eka-ādi-saṃkalita-mita-karaṇī-khaṇḍāni varga-rāśau syus/
children.translated_text: The portions equal to the surds beginning from one onward should be in the square quantity.

children.text: varge karaṇī-tritaye karaṇī-dvitayasya tulya-rūpāṇi//[gīti]
children.translated_text: In the square of three surds, there are pairs of surds equal in form to the pairs of two surds.

children.text: karaṇī-ṣaṭke tisṛṇām daśasu catasṛṇām tithiṣu ca pañcānām/
children.translated_text: In [the square of] six surds, [there are pairs] from three; in [the square of] ten, from four; in fifteen, from five.

children.text: rūpa-kṛtes projjhya padam grāhyam ced anyathā na sat kva api//[gīti]
children.translated_text: One should subtract the root from the square of unity; if [accepted], then [proceed]; otherwise there is no [rational root] anywhere.

children.text: utpatsyamānayā evam mūla-karaṇyā alpayā catur-guṇayā/
children.translated_text: By a small root-surd thus arising, multiplied by four,

children.text: yāsām apavartas syāt rūpa-kṛtes tās viśodhyās syus//[āryā]
children.translated_text: those [surds] whose common factor it would be — from the square of unity those should be subtracted.

children.text: apavarte yās labdhās mūla-karaṇyas bhavanti tās ca api/
children.translated_text: Those obtained after reduction become root-surds as well.

children.text: śeṣa-vidhinā na yadi tās bhavanti mūlam tadā tad asat//[āryā]
children.translated_text: If they do not become [root-surds] by the remaining method, then the root does not exist.

children.text: varge yatra karaṇyas dantais 32 siddhais 24 gajais 8 mitās vidvan/
children.translated_text: In a square where the surds, O learned one, are measured by 32, 24, and 8,

children.text: rūpais daśabhis upetās kim mūlam brūhi tasya syāt//[āryā]
children.translated_text: combined with ten units — tell me, what root should that have?

children.text: varge yatra karaṇyas tithi-viśva-hutāśanais catur-guṇitais/
children.translated_text: In a square where surds equal to 15, 13, and 3, each multiplied by four,

children.text: tulyās daśa-rūpa-āḍhyās kim mūlam brūhi tasya syāt//[āryā]
children.translated_text: combined with ten units — tell me, what root should that have?

children.text: aṣṭau ṣaṣ pañcāśat ṣaṣṭis karaṇī-trayam kṛtau yatra/
children.translated_text: Eight, six, fifty-eight, sixty — three surds in a square, where

children.text: rūpais daśabhis upetam kim mūlam brūhi tasya syāt//[āryā]
children.translated_text: combined with ten units — tell me, what root should that have?

children.text: catur-guṇās sūrya-tithīṣu rudra-nāga-ṛtavas yatra kṛtau karaṇyas/
children.translated_text: Surds multiplied by four, in [quantities of] 12, 15, 11, 8, and 6, where in a square,

children.text: sa-viśava-rūpās vada tad-padam te yadi asti bīje paṭutā-abhimānas//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: combined with 13 units — tell its root, if you pride yourself on skill in algebra.

children.text: catvāriṃśat-aśīti-dviśatī-tulyās karaṇyas ced/
children.translated_text: If surds equal to forty, eighty, and two hundred,

children.text: saptadaśa-rūpa-yuktās tatra krtau kim padam brūhi//[upagīti]
children.translated_text: combined with seventeen units, are in that square — tell me, what is the root?

body.text: kuṭṭaka-vivaraṇam
body.translated_text: Exposition of the Pulverizer (<s>Kuṭṭaka</s>)

children.text: bhājyas hāras kṣepakas ca apavartyas kena api ādau saṃbhave kuṭṭaka-artham/
children.translated_text: The dividend (<s>bhājya</s>), the divisor (<s>hāra</s>), and the additive (<s>kṣepaka</s>) should first be reduced by some [common factor] when possible, for the purpose of the pulverizer.

children.text: yena chinnau bhājya-hārau na tena kṣepas ca etad duṣṭam uddiṣṭam eva//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: If the dividend and divisor are divided by a [factor] that does not also divide the additive — that problem is declared defective.

children.text: parasparam bhājitayos yayos yas śeṣas tayos syāt apavartanam sas/
children.translated_text: When two [numbers] are mutually divided, that remainder which [results] from them is their common factor (<s>apavartana</s>).

children.text: tena apavartena vibhājitau yau tau bhājya-hārau dṛḍha-saṃjñakau stas//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: The [dividend and divisor] divided by that common factor are called 'reduced' (<s>dṛḍha</s>).

children.text: mithas bhajet tau dṛḍha-bhājya-hārau yāvat vibhājye bhavati iha rūpam/
children.translated_text: One should mutually divide the reduced dividend and divisor until the remainder in the dividend becomes unity.

children.text: phalāni adhas adhas tad-adhas niveśyas kṣepas tathā ante kham upāntimena//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: The quotients are placed one below the other, below them the additive, and then zero at the end, beside the penultimate.

children.text: sva-ūrdhve hate antyena yute tad-antyam tyajet muhus syāt iti rāśi-yugmam/
children.translated_text: The last, multiplied by the one above it and added to the one [below] that — discard the last repeatedly; thus a pair of quantities results.

children.text: ūrdhvas vibhājyena dṛḍhena taṣṭas phalam guṇas syāt aparas hareṇa//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: The upper one, reduced by the reduced dividend, gives the quotient (<s>phala</s>), which is the multiplier; the other, [reduced] by the divisor.

children.text: evam tadā eva atra yadā samās tās syus labdhayas ced viṣamās tadānīm/
children.translated_text: This is so when the quotients are even in number; but if they are odd, then

children.text: yathā āgatau labdhi-guṇau viśodhyau sva-takṣaṇāt śeṣa-mitau tu tau stas//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: the quotient and multiplier obtained should be subtracted from their respective reducers — those remainders are the [correct] pair.

children.text: bhavati kuṭṭa-vidhes yuti-bhājyayos samapavartitayos api vā guṇas/
children.translated_text: The multiplier that arises from the pulverizer method when the reduced sum-dividend [is used],

children.text: bhavati yas yuti-bhājakayos punar sas ca bhavet apavartana-saṃguṇas//[drutavilambita]
children.translated_text: also arises when the sum-divisor [is used]; and that is the multiplier multiplied by the common factor.

children.text: yoga-je takṣaṇāt śuddhe guṇa-āptī stas viyoga-je/
children.translated_text: When the [problem] arises from addition, [the results] are obtained by subtracting from the reducer; when from subtraction,

children.text: dhana-bhājya-udbhave tad-vat bhavetām ṛṇa-bhājya-je//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: and when the dividend is positive, likewise; when the dividend is negative, [proceed accordingly].

body.text: guṇa-labdhyos samam grāhyam dhīmatā takṣaṇe phalam/
body.translated_text: The wise person should take the same result of reduction for both multiplier and quotient.

children.text: hara-taṣṭe dhana-kṣepe guṇa-labdhī tu pūrva-vat//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: When the divisor is reduced and the additive is positive, the multiplier and quotient are as before.

children.text: kṣepa-takṣaṇa-lābha-āḍhyā labdhis śuddhau tu varjitā/
children.translated_text: The quotient is increased by the product of the additive and the reducer; but in subtraction, it is diminished.

children.text: atha vā bhāga-hāreṇa taṣṭayos kṣepa-bhājyayos//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, when the additive and dividend are reduced by the divisor,

children.text: guṇas prāk-vat tatas labdhis bhājyāt hata-yuta-uddhṛtāt/
children.translated_text: the multiplier is as before; then the quotient is obtained from the dividend multiplied, added, and divided.

children.text: kṣepa=abhāvas atha vā yatra kṣepas śudhyet hara-uddhṛtas//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Where the additive is zero, or where the additive is exactly divisible by the divisor,

children.text: jñeyas śūnyam guṇas tatra kṣepas hara-hṛtas phalam//[anuṣṭubh-ab; cd=63ab]
children.translated_text: the multiplier should be known as zero there; the additive divided by the divisor is the quotient.

body.text: iṣṭa-āhata-sva-sva-hareṇa yukte te vā bhavetām bahudhā guṇa-āptī//[upajāti-ab; cd=66ab]
body.translated_text: Or, [the multiplier and quotient] multiplied by any desired [number] and increased by any multiple of their respective divisors — they too would be [valid].

children.text: ekaviṃśati-yutam śata-dvayam yad-guṇam gaṇaka pañcaṣaṣṭi-yuj/
children.translated_text: Two hundred twenty-one multiplied by what, O mathematician, added to sixty-five,

children.text: pañca-varjita-śata-dvaya-uddhṛtam śuddhim eti guṇakam vada āśu tam//[rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: and divided by two hundred less five, leaves no remainder? Tell me that multiplier quickly.

children.text: śatam hatam yena yutam navatyā vivarjitam vā vihṛtam triṣaṣṭyā/
children.translated_text: A hundred multiplied by what, added to ninety,

children.text: nir-agrakam syāt vada me guṇam tam spaṣṭam paṭīyān yadi kuṭṭake asi//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: or diminished, and divided by sixty-three, leaves no remainder? Tell me that multiplier, clearly, if you are skilled in the pulverizer.

children.text: yad-guṇā akṣaya-ga-ṣaṣṭis anvitā varjitā ca yadi vā tribhis tatas/
children.translated_text: Sixty-one multiplied by what, when increased or when diminished by three,

children.text: syāt trayodaśa-hṛtā nir-agrakā tam guṇam gaṇaka me pṛthak vada//[rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: and then divided by thirteen, leaves no remainder? Tell me that multiplier separately, O mathematician.

children.text: aṣṭādaśa guṇās kena daśa-āḍhyās vā daśa-ūnitās//[anuṣṭubh-cd; ab=58cd]
children.translated_text: Eighteen multiplied by what, increased or decreased by ten,

children.text: śuddham bhāgam prayacchanti kṣaya-ga-ekādaśa-uddhṛtās/
children.translated_text: gives a pure quotient when divided by sixty-one?

children.text: yena saṃguṇitās pañca trayoviṃśati-saṃyutās//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Five multiplied by what, added to twenty-three,

children.text: varjitās vā tribhis bhaktās nir-agrakās syus sas kas guṇas//[anuṣṭubh-ab; cd=73ab]
children.translated_text: or diminished by three, and divided [as specified], leaves no remainder — what is that multiplier?

children.text: yena pañca guṇitās kha-saṃyutās pañcaṣaṣṭi-sahitās ca te atha vā/
children.translated_text: Five multiplied by what, added to zero, or added to sixty-five,

children.text: syus trayodaśa hṛtā nir-agrakās tam guṇam gaṇaka kīrtaya āśu me//[rathoddhatā]
children.translated_text: and divided by thirteen, leaves no remainder? Tell me that multiplier quickly, O mathematician.

children.text: kṣepam viśuddhim parikalpya rūpam pṛthak tayos ye guṇa-kāra-labdhī//[upajāti-cd; ab=59]
children.translated_text: The additive being made unity as the standard for reduction, the multiplier and quotient for each of the two [are found separately].

children.text: abhīpsita-kṣepa-viśuddhi-nighne sva-hāra-taṣṭe bhavatas tayos te/
children.translated_text: Those [results], multiplied by the desired additive and reduced by their respective divisors, give [the answer].

children.text: kaalpyā atha śuddhis vikalā-avaśeṣam ṣaṣṭis ca bhājyas ku-dināni hāras//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Now let the [quantity to be] reduced have a remainder in minutes (<s>vikalā</s>), and let sixty be the dividend and civil days the divisor.

children.text: tad-jam phalam syus vikalās guṇas tu liptā-agram asmāt ca kalā-lava-agram/
children.translated_text: The resulting quotient gives the minutes, and the multiplier the seconds; and from this, [one gets] the arc-minutes and degrees.

children.text: evam tad-ūrdhvam ca tathā adhimāsa-avama-agrakābhyas divasās ravi-indvos//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Similarly upward [for higher units]; and likewise for intercalary months and omitted days, the days of the sun and moon [are found].

children.text: ekas haras ced guṇakau vibhinnau tadā guṇa-aikyam parikalpya bhājyam/
children.translated_text: If there is one divisor and two different multipliers, then, making the sum of the multipliers the dividend,

children.text: agra-aikyam agram kṛtas ukta-vat yas saṃśliṣṭa-saṃjñas sphuṭa-kuṭṭakas asau//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: and the sum of the remainders the remainder, the pulverizer performed as stated before is called 'combined' (<s>saṃśliṣṭa</s>).

children.text: kas pañca-nighnas vihṛtas triṣaṣṭyā sapta avaśeṣas atha sas eva rāśis/
children.translated_text: What [number], multiplied by five and divided by sixty-three, leaves a remainder of seven? And that same quantity,

children.text: daśa-āhatas syāt vihṛtas triṣaṣṭyā caturdaśa agras vada rāśim enam//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: multiplied by ten and divided by sixty-three, leaves a remainder of fourteen? Tell me that quantity.

body.text: varga-prakṛtis
body.translated_text: Square-Nature (<s>Varga-prakṛti</s>)

children.text: iṣṭam hrasvam tasya vargas prakṛtyā kṣuṇṇas yuktas varjitas vā sas yena/
children.translated_text: Take any desired [number as] the lesser [root]. Its square, multiplied by the coefficient (<s>prakṛti</s>), increased or decreased by [a quantity]

children.text: mūlam dadyāt kṣepakam tam dhana-ṛṇam mūlam tad ca jyeṣṭha-mūlam vadanti//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: that yields a [perfect] root — that [quantity] is called the additive (<s>kṣepaka</s>), positive or negative; and that root is called the greater root.

children.text: hrasva-jyeṣṭha-kṣepakān nyasya teṣām tān anyān vā adhas niveśya krameṇa/
children.translated_text: Setting down the lesser root, greater root, and additive, and below them

children.text: sādhyāni ebhyas bhāvanābhis bahūni mūlāni eṣām bhāvanā procyate atas//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: another [set of the same] or different ones, in order — from these, by the composition (<s>bhāvanā</s>) method, many

children.text: vajra-abhyāsau jyeṣṭha-laghvos tad-aikyam hrasvam laghvos āhatis ca prakṛtyā/
children.translated_text: roots [can be obtained]. The <s>bhāvanā</s> is therefore now explained.

children.text: kṣuṇṇā jyeṣṭha-abhyāsa-yuj jyeṣṭha-mūlam tatra abhyāsas kṣepayos kṣepakas syāt//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: The cross-products of the greater and lesser [roots] — their sum is the [new] lesser [root]. The product of the two lesser [roots], multiplied by the coefficient,

children.text: hrasvam vajra-abhyāsayos antaram vā laghvos ghātas yas prakṛtyā vinighnas/ BH 71k/ ghātas yas ca jyeṣṭhayos tad-viyogas jyeṣṭham kṣepas atra api ca kṣepa-ghātas//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: added to the product of the two greater [roots], is the [new] greater root. The product of the two additives is the [new] additive.

children.text: iṣṭa-varga-hatas kṣepas kṣepas syāt iṣṭa-bhājite/
children.translated_text:
The lesser [root] is the difference of the cross-products, or [alternatively]: the product of the two lesser [roots], multiplied by the coefficient,
subtracted from the product of the two greater [roots] — that difference is the [new] greater [root]. Here too the additive is the product of the additives.

children.text: mūle te stas atha vā kṣepas kṣuṇṇas kṣuṇṇe tadā pade//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: The additive multiplied by the square of any desired [number] becomes the [new] additive; when divided by that desired [number],

children.text: iṣṭa-varga-prakṛtyos yad vivaram tena vā bhajet/[anuṣṭubh-cd; ab=64cd]
children.translated_text: those become the [new] roots. Or the additive is multiplied and the roots are [also] multiplied.

children.text: dvi-ghnam iṣṭam kaniṣṭham tad padam syāt eka-saṃyutau/
children.translated_text: Or divide by the difference between the square of the desired [number] and the coefficient.

children.text: tatas jyeṣṭham iha ānantyam bhāvanātas tathā iṣṭatas//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text:
Twice the desired [number] is the lesser [root]; that root is increased by one.
Then the greater [root] [is found]. Here there are infinitely many [solutions] by composition and by choice.

children.text: kas vargas aṣṭa-hatas sa-ekas kṛtis syāt gaṇaka ucyatām/
children.translated_text: What square, multiplied by eight and increased by one, becomes a [perfect] square? Let it be told, O mathematician.

children.text: ekādaśa-guṇas kas vā vargas sa-ekas kṛtis sakhe//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Or what [number], multiplied by eleven, whose square increased by one, is a [perfect] square, friend?

children.text: hrasva-jyeṣṭha-pada-kṣepān bhājya-prakṣepa-bhājakān/
children.translated_text: Making the lesser root, greater root, and additive into the dividend, additive, and divisor [of a pulverizer],

children.text: kṛtvā kalpyas guṇas tatra tathā prakṛtitas cyute//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: the multiplier should be determined there; likewise when shifted from the coefficient.

children.text: guṇa-varge prakṛti-ūne atha vā alpam śeṣakam yathā/
children.translated_text: In the square of the multiplier, when less than the coefficient, or such that the remainder is small,

children.text: tat tu kṣepa-hṛtam kṣepas vyastas prakṛtitas cyute//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: that [remainder], divided by the additive, is the [new] additive (with reversed sign); [one proceeds] when shifted from the coefficient.

children.text: guṇa-labdhis padam hrasvam tatas jyeṣṭham atas asakṛt/
children.translated_text: The quotient of the multiplier is the [new] lesser root; from that the greater [root is found]. Repeating this,

children.text: tyaktvā pūrva-pada-kṣepān cakra-vālam idam jagus//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: discarding the previous roots and additives — this they call the <s>Cakravāla</s> (cyclic method).

children.text: catur-dvi-eka-yutau evam abhinne bhavatas pade/
children.translated_text: When additives of four, two, or one are thus obtained, the roots for the non-trivial [case result].

children.text: catur-dvi-kṣepa-mūlābhyām rūpa-kṣepa-artha-bhāvanā//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: From the roots for additives of four and two, by composition, [one obtains] the roots for additive one.

children.text: kā saptaṣaṣṭi-guṇitā kṛtis eka-yutā kā ca ekaṣaṣṭi-nihatā ca sakhe sa-rūpā/
children.translated_text: What square, multiplied by sixty-seven, increased by one, is a [perfect] square? And what, multiplied by sixty-one, increased by one, friend?

children.text: syāt mūla-dā yadi kṛti-prakṛtis nitāntam tvad-cetasi pravada tāta tatā-latā-vat//[vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: If the <s>prakṛti</s> (coefficient) of the square yields a root indeed, tell me, dear one, [the answer] like a vine — in your mind! [<s>vasantatilakā</s> meter]

body.text: rūpa-śuddhau khila uddiṣṭam varga-yogas guṇas na ced/
body.translated_text: In the purification of the form, if the product of squares is stated as complete, [and] if not the multiplier,

children.text: akhile kṛti-mūlābhyām dvidhā rūpam vibhājitam//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: from the square and root, the form [is] divided in two ways when incomplete. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: dvidhā hrasva-padam jyeṣṭham tatas rūpa-viśodhane/
children.translated_text: The lesser value [is obtained] from the greater [divided] in two ways; then in the purification of the form,

children.text: pūrvavat vā prasādhyete pade rūpa-viśodhane//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: the two values are to be derived as before, or [else] the forms are purified. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: trayodaśa-guṇas vargas nir-ekas kas kṛtis bhavet/
children.translated_text: What square multiplied by thirteen, diminished by one, would be a perfect square?

children.text: kas vā aṣṭa-guṇitas vargas nir-ekas mūla-das vada//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Or what square multiplied by eight, diminished by one, yields a root? Tell me. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: kas vargas ṣaṣ-guṇas tri-āḍhyas dvādaśa-āḍhyas atha vā kṛtis/
children.translated_text: What square multiplied by six, increased by three, or increased by twelve, is a perfect square?

children.text: yutas vā pañcasaptatyā triśatyā vā kṛtis bhavet//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Or increased by seventy-five, or by three hundred — would be a perfect square? [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: sva-buddhyā eva pade jñeye bahu-kṣepa-viśodhane/
children.translated_text: The two values should be known by one's own intellect through the purification of many additive terms;

children.text: tayos bhāvanayā ānantyam rūpa-kṣepa-pada-utthayā//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: by the <s>bhāvanā</s> (composition) of those [values], there is infinity [of solutions], arising from the values with additive terms of the form. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

body.text: varga-chinne guṇe hrasvam tad-padena vibhājayet/
body.translated_text: When the multiplier is divisible by a square, one should divide the lesser [value] by the root of that [square factor].

body.text: dvātriṃśat-guṇitas vargas kas sa-ekas mūla-das vada//[anuṣṭubh]
body.translated_text: What square multiplied by thirty-two, increased by one, yields a root? Tell me. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: iṣṭa-bhaktas dvidhā kṣepas iṣṭa-ūna-āḍhyas dalī-kṛtas/
children.translated_text: The additive, divided by a chosen [number] and split in two, increased and decreased by the chosen [number], halved,

children.text: guṇa-mūla-hṛtas ca ādyas hrasva-jyeṣṭhe kramāt pade//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: and the first divided by the root of the multiplier — [these give] the lesser and greater values respectively. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: kā kṛtis navabhis kṣuṇṇā dvipañcāśat-yutā kṛtis/
children.translated_text: What perfect square multiplied by nine, with fifty-two added, is a perfect square?

children.text: kas vā catur-guṇas vargas trayastriṃśat-yutā kṛtis//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Or what square multiplied by four, with thirty-three added, is a perfect square? [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: trayodaśa-guṇas vargas kas trayodaśa-varjitas/
children.translated_text: What square multiplied by thirteen, diminished by thirteen,

children.text: trayodaśa-yutas vā syāt vargas eva nigadyatām//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: or increased by thirteen, would itself be a perfect square? State it. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: ṛṇa-gais pañcabhis kṣuṇṇas kas vargas sa-ekaviṃśatis/
children.translated_text: What square multiplied by negative five, with twenty-one added,

children.text: vargas syāt vada ced vetsi kṣaya-ga-prakṛtau vidhim//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: would be a perfect square? Tell me if you know the method for negative multipliers. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: uktam bīja-upayogī idam saṃkṣiptam gaṇitam kila/
children.translated_text: What has been stated [so far] is the arithmetic useful for algebra, in brief indeed.

children.text: atas bījam pravakṣyāmi gaṇaka-ānanda-kārakam//[anuṣṭubh]
children.translated_text: Henceforth I shall expound the algebra (<s>bīja</s>) that delights mathematicians. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

body.text: eka-varṇa-samī-karaṇam
body.translated_text: Equations in one unknown

children.text: yāvattāvat kalpyam avyakta-rāśes mānam tasmin kurvatā uddiṣṭam eva/
children.translated_text: For an unknown quantity, as much as is needed (<s>yāvattāvat</s>) should be assumed as its measure; with that, performing the stated [operations],

children.text: tulyau pakṣau sādhanīyau prayatnāt tyaktvā kṣiptvā vā api saṃguṇya bhaktvā//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: the two sides [of the equation] should be made equal with effort — by subtracting, adding, multiplying, or dividing. [<s>śālinī</s> meter]

children.text: eka-avyaktam śodhayet anya-pakṣāt rūpāṇi anyasya itarasmāt ca pakṣāt/
children.translated_text: The single unknown should be cleared from the other side, and the known quantities (<s>rūpa</s>) [cleared] from the other side likewise.

children.text: śeṣa-avyakte na uddharet rūpa-śeṣam vyaktam mānam jāyate vyakta-rāśes//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: The remainder of known quantities divided by the remainder of unknowns — the known measure of the unknown quantity is [thus] obtained. [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text: avyaktānām dvi-ādikānām api iha yāvattāvat dvi-ādi-nighnam hṛtam vā/
children.translated_text: For two or more unknowns also, here, as much as is needed, multiplied by two or more, or divided,

children.text: yukta-ūnam vā kalpayet ātma-buddhyā mānam kva api vyaktam evam viditvā//[śālinī]
children.translated_text: or increased or decreased, one should assume by one's own intellect; the known measure [is found] somewhere in this way. [<s>śālinī</s>]

children.text: ekasya rūpa-triśatī ṣaṭ aśvās aśvās daśa anyasya tu tulya-maulyās/
children.translated_text: One [person] has three hundred <s>rūpa</s>s (coins) and six horses; the other has ten horses of equal value,

children.text: ṛṇam tathā rūpa-śatam ca yasya tau tulya-vittau ca kim aśva-maulyam//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: and a debt of one hundred <s>rūpa</s>s — and the two have equal wealth. What is the price of a horse? [<s>upajāti</s> meter]

children.text: yat ādya-vittasya dalam dvi-yuktam tad-tulya-vittas yadi vā dvitīyas/
children.translated_text: If half of the first one's wealth plus two equals the wealth of the second;

children.text: ādyas dhanena tri-guṇas anyatas vā pṛthak pṛthak me vada vāji-maulyam//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: or the first has triple the wealth of the other — tell me separately the price of the horse. [<s>upajāti</s>]

children.text: māṇikya-amala-nīla-mauktika-mitis pañca aṣṭa sapta kramāt ekasya anyatarasya sapta nava ṣaṭ tad-ratna-saṃkhyā sakhe/
children.translated_text: The count of rubies, fine sapphires, and pearls is five, eight, seven respectively for one [merchant]; for the other, seven, nine, six — those being the gem counts, friend.

children.text: rūpāṇām navatis dvi-ṣaṣṭis anayos tau tulya-vittau tathā bīja-jña prati-ratna-jāni su-mate maulyāni śīghram vada//[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: Their [total] values are ninety and sixty-two <s>rūpa</s>s — they have equal wealth. O knower of algebra, tell me quickly the price of each type of gem, wise one! [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: ekas bravīti mama dehi atam dhanena tvattas bhavāmi hi sakhe dvi-guṇas tatas anyas/
children.translated_text: One says: 'Give me a hundred from your wealth, friend, and I shall be twice as rich as you.' The other

children.text: brūte daśa arpayasi ced mama ṣaṣ-guṇas aham tvattas tayos vada dhane mama kim-pramāṇe//[siṃhoddhatā]
children.translated_text: says: 'If you give me ten, I shall be six times as rich as you.' Tell me the wealth of each — what are their amounts? [<s>siṃhoddhatā</s>]

children.text: māṇikya-aṣṭakam indranīla-daśakam muktāphalānām śatam yat te karṇa-vibhūṣaṇe sama-dhanam krītam tvad-arthe mayā/
children.translated_text: Eight rubies, ten sapphires, a hundred pearls — these I bought for you as ear-ornaments, my dear, at equal cost to your [ornaments].

children.text: tad-ratna-traya-maulya-saṃyuti-mitis tri-ūnam śata-ardham priye maulyam brūhi pṛthak yadi iha gaṇite kalpā asi kalyāṇini//[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: The sum of the prices of those three types of gems is half a hundred less three. O lovely one, tell me the separate prices if you are skilled in arithmetic! [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: pañca-aṃśas ali-kulāt kadambam agamat tri-aṃśas śilīndhram tayos viśleṣas tri-guṇas mṛga-akṣi kuṭajam dolāyamānas aparas/
children.translated_text: One-fifth of a swarm of bees went to a <s>kadamba</s> flower, one-third to a <s>śilīndhra</s>; three times the difference of those [two groups], O doe-eyed one, went to a <s>kuṭaja</s> flower, and one more, swaying,

children.text: kānte ketaka-mālatī-parimala-prāpta-eka-kāla-priyāt dūta-āhūtas itas tatas bhramati khe bhṛṅgas ali-saṃkhyām vada//[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: enticed by the fragrance of <s>ketaka</s> and <s>mālatī</s>, summoned by a beloved arrived at the same time — it wanders here and there in the sky. Tell the number of bees in the swarm. [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: pañcaka-śata-datta-dhanāt phalasya vargam viśodhya pariśiṣṭam/
children.translated_text: From a capital of five hundred, subtract the square of the interest; the remainder

children.text: dattam daśaka-śatena tulyas kālas phalam ca tayos//[āryā]
children.translated_text: lent at one hundred [per cent] — the time and interest of the two are equal. [<s>āryā</s>]

children.text: eka-śata-datta-dhanāt phalasya vargam viśodhya pariśiṣṭam/
children.translated_text: From a capital of one hundred, subtract the square of the interest; the remainder

children.text: pañcaka-śatena dattam tulyas kālas phalam ca tayos//[āryā]
children.translated_text: lent at five hundred — the time and interest of the two are equal. [<s>āryā</s>]

children.text: māṇikya-aṣṭakam indranīla-daśakam muktāphalānām śatam sat-vajrāṇi ca pañca ratna-vaṇijām yeṣām caturṇām dhanam/
children.translated_text: Eight rubies, ten sapphires, a hundred pearls, and five good diamonds — these are the wealth of four gem-merchants.

children.text: saṅga-sneha-vaśena te nija-dhanāt dattvā ekam ekam mithas jātās tulya-dhanās pṛthak vada sakhe tad-ratna-maulyāni me//[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: Out of affection and friendship, each giving one [gem] to the others from his own wealth, they became equal in wealth. Tell me separately, friend, the prices of those gems. [<s>śārdūlavikrīḍita</s>]

children.text: pañcaka-śatena dattam mūlam sa-kalāntaram gate varṣe/
children.translated_text: Capital lent at five hundred; after one year with accumulated interest,

children.text: dvi-guṇam ṣoḍaśa-hīnam labdham kim mūlam ācakṣva//[āryā]
children.translated_text: the amount obtained is double minus sixteen. Tell me what the capital was. [<s>āryā</s>]

children.text: yat pañcaka-dvika-catuṣka-śatena dattam khaṇḍais tribhis navati-yuj triśatī dhanam tat/
children.translated_text: That which was lent in three installments at five hundred, two hundred, and four hundred — the total wealth is three hundred ninety.

children.text: māseṣu sapta-daśa-pañcasu tulyam āptam khaṇḍa-traye api sa-phalam vada khaṇḍa-saṃkhyām// [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: The interest obtained in five, seventeen, [and] ten months is equal for the three installments. Tell the amounts of the installments. [<s>vasantatilakā</s>]

children.text: pura-praveśe daśa-das dvi-saṃguṇam vidhāya śeṣam daśa-bhuk ca nirgame/
children.translated_text: On entering a city, he gave ten and doubled the remainder; on leaving, he also spent ten.

children.text: dadau daśa evam nagara-traye abhavat tri-nighnam ādyam vada tat kiyat dhanam//
children.translated_text: He gave ten in the same way in three cities; [the remainder was] triple the original. Tell me, what was the [initial] amount of money?

children.text: sa=ardham tandula-mānaka-trayam aho drammeṇa māna-aṣṭakam mudgānām ca yadi trayodaśa-mitās etās vaṇik kākiṇīs/
children.translated_text: Three measures of rice for half a <s>dramma</s>, eight measures of <s>mudga</s> (green gram) for one <s>dramma</s>, and if these thirteen <s>kākiṇī</s>s [be taken] by the merchant —

children.text: ādāya arpaya tandula-aṃśa-yugalam mudga-eka-bhāga-anvitam kṣipram kṣipra-bhujas vrajema hi yutas sa-arthas agratas yāsyati//
children.translated_text: having taken [them], give two shares of rice mixed with one share of <s>mudga</s>. Quickly, let us proceed together with profit — the one with provisions shall go ahead!

children.text: sva-ardha-pañca-aṃśa-navamais yuktās ke syus samās trayas/
children.translated_text: What three [numbers] increased by one-half, one-fifth, and one-ninth of [each other] are equal?

children.text: anya-aṃśa-dvaya-hīnās ye ṣaṣṭi-śeṣās ca tān vada//
children.translated_text: And those decreased by two shares of the other, with sixty as remainder — tell those. [<s>anuṣṭubh</s>]

children.text: trayodaśa tathā pañca karaṇyau bhujayos mitī/
children.translated_text: Thirteen and five <s>karaṇī</s>s (surds) are the measures of the two sides;

children.text: bhūs ajñātā atra catvāras phalam bhūmim vada āśu me//
children.translated_text: the base is unknown; here [the area] is four. Tell me quickly the area and the base!

children.text: daśa-pañca-karaṇī-antaram ekas bāhus paras ca ṣaṭ karaṇī/
children.translated_text: The difference of the surds ten and five is one side; the other is the surd of six.

children.text: bhūs aṣṭādaśa karaṇī rūpa-ūnā lambam ācakṣva//
children.translated_text: The base is the surd of eighteen minus one. Tell me the altitude.

children.text: asamāna-sama-chedān rāśīn tān caturas vada/
children.translated_text: Tell those four quantities with unequal and equal denominators

children.text: yad-aikyam yad-ghana-aikyam vā yeṣām varg-aikya-saṃmitam// [āpaṭe: -dhana- < -ghana-]
children.translated_text: whose sum equals their sum of cubes, or whose sum of squares [equals the same].

children.text: tri-asra-kṣetrasya yasya syāt phalam karṇena saṃmitam/
children.translated_text: Of what triangle would the area be equal to its hypotenuse?

children.text: dos-koṭi-śruti-ghātena samam yasya ca tad-vat//
children.translated_text: And of what [triangle] would [the area] be equal to the product of the arm, upright, and hypotenuse?

children.text: yutau vargas antare vargas yayos ghāte ghanas bhavet/
children.translated_text: The sum [of two quantities] when squared [gives a result], their difference when squared [gives a result], and their product is a cube.

children.text: tau rāśī śīghram ācakṣva dakṣas asi gaṇite yadi//
children.translated_text: Tell those two quantities quickly, if you are skilled in arithmetic.

children.text: ghana-aikyam jāyate vargas varga-aikyam ca yayos ghanas/
children.translated_text: The sum of whose cubes is a square, and the sum of whose squares is a cube —

children.text: tau ced vetsi tadā aham tvām manye bīja-vidām varam//
children.translated_text: if you know those [two quantities], then I consider you the best among those who know algebra.

children.text: yatra tri-asre kṣetre dhātrī manu-saṃmitā sakhe bāhū/
children.translated_text: In a triangle, friend, the two sides measure according to the earth and <s>Manu</s> [fourteen],

children.text: ekas pañcadaśa anyas trayodaśa vada avalambakam tatra//
children.translated_text: one [being] fifteen, the other thirteen — tell the altitude in that [triangle].

children.text: yadi sama-bhuvi veṇus dvi-tri-pāṇi-pramāṇas gaṇaka pavana-vegāt eka-deśe su-bhagnas/
children.translated_text: If on level ground a bamboo two-and-three-quarter hands [in height], O mathematician, is broken at one point by the force of the wind,

children.text: bhuvi nṛpa-mita-hasteṣu aṅga lagnam tad-agram kathaya katiṣu mūlāt eṣas bhagnas kareṣu//
children.translated_text: and its tip touches the ground at a distance of [certain] king-measured hands — tell me at how many hands from the root is it broken?

children.text: cakra-krauñca-ākulita-salile kva api dṛṣṭam taḍāge toyāt ūrdhvam kamala-kalikā-agram vitasti-pramāṇam/
children.translated_text: In a lake disturbed by <s>cakra</s> birds and herons, a lotus bud was seen somewhere, its tip one span above the water.

children.text: mandam mandam calitam anilena āhatam hasta-yugme tasmin magnam gaṇaka kathaya kṣipram ambu-pramāṇam//
children.translated_text: Slowly, slowly, moved by the striking wind, it submerged at a distance of two hands. O mathematician, tell quickly the depth of the water!

children.text: vṛkṣāt hasta-śata-ucchrayāt śata-yuge vāpīm kapis kas api agāt uttīrya atha paras drutam śruti-pathāt proḍḍīya kiṃcit drumāt/ [āpaṭe: kiṃci < kiṃcit]
children.translated_text: From a tree a hundred hands high, a monkey descended and went to a well at a distance of a hundred [hands]; then another [monkey] quickly flew up a little from the tree along a hypotenuse path.

children.text: jātā evam samatā tayos yadi gatau uḍḍīya-mānam kiyat vidvan ced su-pariśramas asti gaṇite kṣipram tat ācakṣva me//
children.translated_text: If the distances traveled by the two became equal — how far [did the second] fly up? O learned one, if you have great diligence in mathematics, tell me that quickly!

children.text: pañcadaśa-daśa-kara-ucchrāya-veṇvos ajñāta-madhya-bhūmikayos/
children.translated_text: Of two bamboos of heights fifteen and ten hands, with the ground between them unknown,

children.text: itaretara-mūla-agra-ga-sūtra-yutes lamba-mānam ācakṣva//
children.translated_text: with strings going from each base to the other's top — tell the measure of the altitude [where they cross].

body.text: madhyama-āharaṇam
body.translated_text: Middle extraction (<s>madhyamāharaṇa</s>)

children.text: avyakta-varga-ādi yadā avaśeṣam pakṣau tadā iṣṭena nihatya kiṃcit/
children.translated_text: When, after [operations], the square or higher [power] of the unknown remains on the two sides, then by multiplying both [sides] by some chosen [quantity],

children.text: kṣepyam tayos yena pada-pradas syāt avyakta-pakṣasya padena bhūyas//
children.translated_text: something should be added to both so that one side yields a root; by the root of the unknown-side, again [proceed].

children.text: vyaktasya pakṣasya sama-kriyā evam avyakta-mānam khalu labhyate tat/
children.translated_text: By the same operations on the known (<s>vyakta</s>) side, the unknown (<s>avyakta</s>) measure is indeed obtained;

children.text: na nirvahas ced ghana-varga-vargeṣu evam tadā jñeyam idam sva-buddhyā//
children.translated_text: if there is no solution in cubes and fourth powers, then this should be understood by one's own intellect.

children.text: avyakta-mūla-ṛṇa-ga-rūpatas alpam vyaktasya pakṣasya padam yadi syāt/
children.translated_text: If the root of the known side is less by the unknown root, the negative quantity, and the absolute number,

children.text: ṛṇam dhanam tat ca vidhāya sādhyam avyakta-mānam dvi-vidham kvacit tat//
children.translated_text: making that negative or positive as appropriate, the unknown measure is to be determined — it may be twofold in some cases.

children.text: catur-āhata-varga-samais rūpais pakṣa-dvayam guṇayet/
children.translated_text: Multiply both sides by the absolute numbers equal to four times the [coefficient of the] square;

children.text: pūrva-avyaktasya kṛtes sama-rūpāṇi kṣipet tayos eva//
children.translated_text: and add to both sides the absolute numbers equal to the square of the original [coefficient of the] unknown.

children.text: ali-kula-dala-mūlam mālatīm yātam aṣṭau nikhila-navama-bhāgās cālinī bhṛṅgam ekam/
children.translated_text: The square root of half a swarm of bees went to <s>mālatī</s> flowers; eight-ninths of the whole formed a line of bees; one bee,

children.text: niśi parimala-lubdham padma-madhye niruddham pratiraṇati raṇantam brūhi kānte ali-saṃkhyām//
children.translated_text: attracted by fragrance at night, was trapped in the middle of a lotus — it buzzes in reply to the buzzing one — tell, O beloved, the number of bees.

children.text: pārthas karṇa-vadhāya mārgaṇa-gaṇam kruddhas raṇe saṃdadhe tasya ardhena nivārya tad-śara-gaṇam mūlais caturbhis hayān/
children.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), angered in battle, fitted an array of arrows for the slaying of <s>Karṇa</s>; with half of those he warded off <s>Karṇa</s>'s arrows; with four square roots he struck the horses;

children.text: śalyam ṣaḍbhis atha iṣubhis tribhis api chatram dhvajam kārmukam ciccheda asya śiras śareṇa kati te yān arjunas saṃdadhe//
children.translated_text: with six arrows <s>Śalya</s>, with three arrows the umbrella, banner, and bow; he cut off his head with one arrow — how many arrows did <s>Arjuna</s> fit?

children.text: vi-ekasya gacchasya dalam kila ādis ādes dalam tad-pracayas phalam ca/
children.translated_text: The first term of a series is the common difference diminished by one; the first term is the common difference; the product of that is the result;

children.text: caya-ādi-gaccha-abhihatis sva-sapta-bhāga-adhikā brūhi caya-ādi-gacchān//
children.translated_text: the product of the common difference, first term, and number of terms, increased by seven-sevenths of itself — tell the common difference, first term, and number of terms.

children.text: kas khena vihṛtas rāśis koṭyā yuktas atha vā ūnitas/
children.translated_text: What quantity, multiplied by zero, then increased or diminished by a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million),

children.text: vargitas sva-padena āḍhyas kha-guṇas navatis bhavet//
children.translated_text: squared, increased by its own root, and multiplied by zero, becomes ninety?

children.text: kas sva-ardha-sahitas rāśis kha-guṇas vargitas yutas/
children.translated_text: What quantity, together with its own half, multiplied by zero, squared, increased by

children.text: sva-padābhyām sva-bhaktas ca jātas pañcadaśa ucyatām//
children.translated_text: its own two roots, divided by itself, becomes fifteen — let it be stated.

children.text: rāśis dvādaśa-nighnas rāśi-ghana-āḍhyas ca kas samas yasya/
children.translated_text: What quantity, multiplied by twelve and increased by the cube of the quantity, equals that of which

children.text: rāśi-kṛtis ṣaṣ-guṇitā pañcatriṃśat-yutā vidvan//
children.translated_text: the square of the quantity multiplied by six plus thirty-five, O learned one?

children.text: kas rāśis dviśatī-kṣuṇṇas rāśi-varga-yutas hatas/
children.translated_text: What quantity, multiplied by two hundred, increased by the square of the quantity, multiplied

children.text: dvābhyām tena ūnitas rāśi-varga-vargas ayutam 10000 bhavet/
children.translated_text: by two, diminished by the fourth power of the quantity, becomes ten thousand?

children.text: rūpa-ūnam vada tam rāśim vetsi bīja-kriyām yadi//
children.translated_text: Tell that quantity diminished by one, if you know the algebra (<s>bījakriyā</s>).

children.text: vana-antarāle plavaga-aṣṭa-bhāgas saṃvargitas valgati jāta-rāgas/
children.translated_text: In the midst of a forest, one-eighth of a troop of monkeys, squared, leaps about, seized by passion;

children.text: brūt-kāra-nāda-pratināda-hṛṣṭās dṛṣṭās girau dvādaśa te kiyantas//
children.translated_text: delighted by the echo of roaring sounds, twelve are seen on a mountain — how many are they?

children.text: yūthāt pañca-aṃśakas tri-ūnas vargitas gahvaram gatas/
children.translated_text: One-fifth of a troop diminished by three, squared, has gone into a cave;

children.text: dṛṣṭas śākhā-mṛgas śākhām ārūḍhas vada te kati/
children.translated_text: one monkey is seen climbing a branch — tell, how many are they?

children.text: karṇasya tri-lavena ūnā dvādaśa-aṅgula-śaṅku-bhā/
children.translated_text: The shadow of a twelve-<s>aṅgula</s> (finger-breadth) gnomon, diminished by three-tenths of the hypotenuse,

children.text: caturdaśa-aṅgulā jātā gaṇaka brūhi tām drutam//
children.translated_text: becomes fourteen <s>aṅgulas</s> — O calculator, tell that quickly.

children.text: catvāras rāśayas ke te mūla-dās ye dvi-saṃyutās
children.translated_text: What are those four quantities which, when increased by two, yield roots,

children.text: dvayos dvayos yathā āsanna-ghātās ca aṣṭādaśa-anvitās/
children.translated_text: and whose products taken two by two, when increased by eighteen,

children.text: mūla-dās sarva-mūla-aikyāt ekādaśa-yutāt padam/
children.translated_text: yield roots; from the sum of all roots increased by eleven, the root

children.text: trayodaśa sakhe jātam bīja-jña vada tān mama//
children.translated_text: is thirteen, O friend — O knower of algebra, tell me those.

children.text: rāśi-kṣepāt vadha-kṣepas yad-guṇas tat pada-uttaram/
children.translated_text: From the additive of the quantity, the additive of the product is obtained; what multiplies that is increased by the root.

children.text: avyakta-rāśayas kalpyās vargitās kṣepa-varjitās//
children.translated_text: Unknown quantities are to be assumed, squared, and diminished by the additive.

children.text: kṣetre tithi-nakhais tulye dos-koṭī tatra kā śrutis/
children.translated_text: In a right triangle (<s>kṣetra</s>) with [hypotenuse] fifteen and [area] twenty, what are the base (<s>dos</s>) and perpendicular (<s>koṭi</s>)? Let the derivation be stated,

children.text: upapattis ca rūḍhasya gaṇitasya asya kathyatām//
children.translated_text: and the proof of this established computation be given.

children.text: dos-koṭi-antara-vargeṇa dvi-ghnas ghātas samanvitas/
children.translated_text: The square of the difference of the base and perpendicular, together with twice their product,

children.text: varga-yoga-samas sas syāt dvayos avyaktayos yathā//
children.translated_text: equals the sum of their squares — this holds for two unknowns, as follows:

children.text: bhujāt tri-ūnāt padam vi-ekam koṭi-karṇa-antaram sakhe/
children.translated_text: Where the root of the base diminished by three, minus one, is the difference of the perpendicular and hypotenuse, O friend —

children.text: yatra tatra vada kṣetre dos-koṭi-śravaṇān mama//
children.translated_text: in that field, tell me the base, perpendicular, and hypotenuse.

children.text: varga-yogasya yad-rāśyos yuti-vargasya ca antaram/
children.translated_text: The difference between the sum of squares of two quantities and the square of their sum

children.text: dvi-ghna-ghāta-samānam syāt dvayos avyaktayos yathā/
children.translated_text: is equal to twice their product — for two unknowns, as follows:

children.text: catur-guṇasya ghātasya yuti-vargasya ca antaram/
children.translated_text: The difference between the square of the sum and four times the product

children.text: rāśi-antara-kṛtes tulyam dvayos avyaktayos yathā//
children.translated_text: is equal to the square of the difference of the two quantities — for two unknowns, as follows:

children.text: catvāriṃśat yutis yeṣām dos-koṭi-śravasām vada/
children.translated_text: Tell those base, perpendicular, and hypotenuse whose sum is forty,

children.text: bhuja-koṭi-vadhas yeṣu śatam viṃśati-saṃyutam//
children.translated_text: and in which the product of the base and perpendicular is one hundred and twenty.

children.text: yogas dos-koṭi-karṇānām ṣaṭpañcāśat 56 vadhas tathā/
children.translated_text: The sum of the base, perpendicular, and hypotenuse is fifty-six; the product is

children.text: ṣaṭśatī saptabhis kṣuṇṇā 4200 yeṣām tān me pṛthak vada//
children.translated_text: six hundred multiplied by seven, that is 4200 — tell me those separately.

body.text: aneka-varṇa-samīkaraṇam
body.translated_text: Equations with multiple unknowns (<s>anekavarṇa-samīkaraṇa</s>)

children.text: ādyam varṇam śodhayet anya-pakṣāt anyān rūpāṇi anyatas ca ādya-bhakte/
children.translated_text: Eliminate the first unknown from the other side; the other unknowns and the absolute numbers from the other side; divided by the first,

children.text: pakṣe anyasmin ādya-varṇa-unmitis syāt varṇasya ekasya unmitīnām bahutve//
children.translated_text: in the other side the measure of the first unknown is obtained. When there are many values for one unknown,

children.text: samī-kṛta-cheda-game tu tābhyas tad-anya-varṇa-unmitayas prasādhyās/
children.translated_text: in the equation reduced to equal denominators, the measures of the other unknowns are to be determined from those;

children.text: antya-unmitau kuṭṭaka-vidhes guṇa-āptī te bhājya-tad-bhājaka-varna-māne//
children.translated_text: in the last unknown, the multiplier and quotient of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (pulverizer) method give the measures of the dividend-unknown and divisor-unknown.

children.text: anye api bhājye yadi santi varṇās tad-mānam iṣṭam parikalpya sādhye/
children.translated_text: If there are other unknowns in the dividend, assuming their measure at will, one should solve;

children.text: vilomaka-uttāpana-tas anya-varṇa-mānāni bhinnam yadi mānam evam/
children.translated_text: by the methods of reversal and substitution, the measures of the other unknowns [are found]. If the measure is fractional,

children.text: bhūyas kāryas kuṭṭake atra antya-varṇam tena utthāpya utthāpayet vyastam ādyāt//
children.translated_text: the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> should be applied again; having thereby raised the last unknown, one should raise the others in reverse order from the first.

children.text: māṇikya-amala-nīla-mauktika-mitis pañca aṣṭa sapta kramāt ekasya anyatarasya sapta nava ṣaṭ tad-ratna-saṃkhyā sakhe/
children.translated_text: The quantities of rubies, pure sapphires, and pearls are five, eight, and seven respectively for one person, and seven, nine, and six for another, O friend;

children.text: rūpāṇām navatis dviṣaṣṭis anayos tau tulya-vittau tathā bīja-jña prati-ratna-jāni sumate maulyāni śīghram vada// [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: the [total prices in] absolute numbers are ninety and sixty-two for these two of equal wealth — O knower of algebra, tell me quickly the prices of each gem, O wise one.

children.text: ekas bravīti mama dehi śatam dhanena tvattas bhavāmi hi sakhe dvi-guṇas tatas anyas/
children.translated_text: One says: 'Give me a hundred from your wealth, and I become double of you, O friend;'

children.text: brūte daśa arpayasi ced mama ṣaṣ-guṇas aham tvattas tayos vada dhane mama kim-pramāṇe//
children.translated_text: the other says: 'If you give me ten, I become six times you' — tell me the measure of their wealth.

children.text: aśvās pañca-guṇa-aṅga-maṅgala-mitās yeṣām caturṇām dhanāni uṣṭrās ca dvi-muni-śruti-kṣiti-mitās aṣṭa-dvi-bhū-pāvakās/
children.translated_text: Horses costing five, two, eight, and seven respectively; camels costing two, seven, four, and three;

children.text: teṣām aśvatarās vṛṣās muni-mahī-netra-indu-saṃkhyās kramāt sarve tulya-dhanās ca te vada sapadi aśva-ādi-maulyāni me//
children.translated_text: mules and bulls costing seven, one, two, and one respectively — all having equal total wealth — tell me at once the prices of horses and the rest.

children.text: tribhis pārāvatās pañca pañcabhis sapta sārasās/
children.translated_text: Three pigeons for five, five cranes for seven,

children.text: saptabhis nava haṃsās ca navabhis barhiṇas trayas//
children.translated_text: seven swans for nine, and nine peacocks for three

children.text: drammais avāpyate dramma-śatena śatam ānaya/
children.translated_text: <s>drammas</s> (coins) — with one hundred <s>drammas</s>, obtain one hundred [birds];

children.text: eṣām pārāvata-ādīnām vinoda-artham mahī-pates//
children.translated_text: bring these pigeons and the rest for the amusement of the king.

children.text: ṣaṣ-bhaktas pañca-agras pañca-vibhaktas bhavet catuṣka-agras/
children.translated_text: What number, divided by six, leaves remainder five; divided by five, leaves remainder four;

children.text: catur-uddhṛtas trika-agras dvi-agras tri-samuddhṛtas kas syāt//
children.translated_text: divided by four, leaves remainder three; divided by three, leaves remainder two?

children.text: syus pañca-sapta-navabhis kṣuṇṇeṣu hṛteṣu keṣu viṃśatyā/
children.translated_text: What numbers, when multiplied by five, seven, and nine and divided by twenty,

children.text: rūpa-uttarāṇi śeṣāṇi avāptayas ca api śeṣa-samās//
children.translated_text: leave remainders increasing by one, and the quotients are also equal to the remainders?

children.text: eka-agras dvi-hṛtas kas syāt dvika-agras tri-samuddhṛtas/
children.translated_text: What number, divided by two, leaves remainder one; divided by three, leaves remainder two;

children.text: trika-agras pañcabhis bhaktas tad-vat eva hi labdhayas//
children.translated_text: divided by five, leaves remainder three — and the quotients are likewise equal?

children.text: kau rāśī vada pañca-ṣaṭka-vihṛtau eka-dvika-agrau yayos dvi-agram tri-uddhṛtam antaram nava-hṛtā pañca-agrakā syāt yutis/
children.translated_text: Tell those two quantities which, divided by five and six, leave remainders one and two; whose difference, divided by three, leaves remainder two; whose sum, divided by nine, leaves remainder five;

children.text: ghātas sapta-hṛtas ṣaṣ-agras iti tau ṣaṭka-aṣṭakābhyām vinā vidvan kuṭṭaka-vedi-kuñjara-ghaṭā-saṃghaṭṭa-sṃhas asi ced//
children.translated_text: whose product, divided by seven, leaves remainder six — without six and eight — O learned one, you are a lion among elephants clashing at the tank of <s>kuṭṭaka</s> knowledge, if you can do this!

children.text: navabhis saptabhis kṣuṇṇas kas rāśis triṃśatā hṛtas/
children.translated_text: What quantity, multiplied by nine and seven, divided by thirty,

children.text: yat agra-aikyam phala-aikya-āḍhyam bhavet ṣaḍviṃśates mitam//
children.translated_text: gives the sum of remainders plus the sum of quotients equal to twenty-six?

children.text: kas tri-sapta-nava-kṣuṇṇas rāśis triṃśat-vibhājitas/
children.translated_text: What quantity, multiplied by three, seven, and nine, divided by thirty,

children.text: yat agra-aikyam api triṃśat-hṛtam ekādaśa-agrakam//
children.translated_text: gives the sum of remainders, also divided by thirty, leaving remainder eleven?

children.text: kas trayoviṃśati-kṣuṇṇas ṣaṣṭyā asītyā hṛtas pṛthak/
children.translated_text: What quantity, multiplied by twenty-three, divided separately by sixty and eighty,

children.text: yat agra-aikyam śatam dṛṣṭam kuṭṭaka-jña vada āśu tam//
children.translated_text: gives the sum of remainders equal to one hundred — O knower of <s>kuṭṭaka</s>, tell that quickly.

children.text: atra adhikasya varṇasya bhājyasthasya īpsitā mitis/
children.translated_text: The desired measure of the additional unknown present in the dividend

children.text: bhāga-labdhasya no kalpyā kriyā vyabhicaret tathā//
children.translated_text: should not be assumed for the quotient obtained — otherwise the procedure would go astray.

children.text: kas pañca-guṇitas rāśis trayodaśa-vibhājitas/
children.translated_text: What quantity, multiplied by five, divided by thirteen,

children.text: yat labdham rāśinā yuktam triṃśat jātam vada āśu tam//
children.translated_text: gives a quotient which, added to the quantity, equals thirty — tell that quickly.

children.text: ṣaṣ-aṣṭa-śatakās krītvā sama-ardhena phalāni ye/
children.translated_text: Those who buy six, eight, and one hundred [fruits] at the same [total] price and,

children.text: vikrīya ca punar śeṣam eka-ekam pañcabhis paṇais/
children.translated_text: selling the remainder at one each for five <s>paṇas</s> (coins),

children.text: jātās sama-paṇās teṣām kas krayas vikrayas ca kas//
children.translated_text: end up with equal amounts of money — what is their buying price and selling price?

body.text: aneka-varṇa-samī-karaṇa-antar-gatam madhyama-āharaṇam
body.translated_text: The intermediate equation (<s>madhyamāharaṇa</s>) within multi-variable equations

children.text: varga-ādyam ced tulya-śuddhau kṛtāyām pakṣasya ekasya ukta-vat varga-mūlam/
children.translated_text: If, after performing equal subtraction on both sides, the square-leading [expression] remains, then take the square root of one side as before;

children.text: varga-prakṛtyā para-pakṣa-mūlam tayos samī-kāra-vidhis punar ca/
children.translated_text: by the method of the square-nature (<s>vargaprakṛti</s>), find the root of the other side; then equate the two again.

children.text: varga-prakṛtyā viṣayas na ced syāt tadā anya-varṇsya kṛtes samam tam//
children.translated_text: If the square-nature method does not apply, then set it equal to the square of another unknown;

children.text: kṛtvā aparam pakṣam atha anya-mānam kṛti-prakṛtyā ādya-mitis tathā ca/
children.translated_text: making the other side, then determine the other unknown's measure by the square-nature of the square; likewise

children.text: varga-prakṛtyā viṣayas yathā syāt tathā sudhībhis bahudhā vicintyam//
children.translated_text: so that the square-nature method applies — this should be considered in many ways by the wise.

children.text: bījam matis vividha-varṇa-sahāyinī hi manda-avabodhavidhaye vibudhais nija-ādyais/
children.translated_text: Algebra (<s>bīja</s>) is indeed the intellect accompanied by various unknowns (<s>varṇas</s>); for the instruction of the slow-witted, by the wise ancients

children.text: vistāritā
children.translated_text: it was elaborated.
